rationale: Section 10.2(a) imposes a symmetric consent requirement on our Depositor and on Cellco as Servicer, but expressly carves out Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6. Section 5.3 lets the Depositor's merger/consolidation counterparty, business successor, or an Affiliate assignee become the successor Depositor without consent (notice/officer's certificate and opinions only), which is the affiliate/successor M&A carve-out the playbook requires; Section 7.6 gives Cellco the mirror-image treatment. The Issuer is not restricted at all, and Section 2.2 acknowledges the Issuer's assignment and pledge of the Depositor Transferred Property to the Indenture Trustee for the Secured Parties, so our financing-side transfers are preserved and Section 10.2(b) binds permitted successors and assigns. There is no change-of-control trigger anywhere in the document (no "change of control" language), and Section 7.1 is a "No Resignation" covenant barring Cellco from resigning unless legally unable to perform, so the counterparty has no exit or re-pricing right on our reorganisation — the walk-away scenarios are absent. Two points short of the pure preferred position are noted rather than flagged: the third-party consent gate is not expressed as "not to be unreasonably withheld" and there is no competitor bar on a Servicer assignment (both are structural noteholder/rating-agency protections in a securitization and apply symmetrically), and Section 6.4 permits Cellco free delegation while it is Servicer or Custodian — acceptable because no delegation or contracting relieves it of responsibility for those obligations. On its material terms the package sits at or above the fallback (mutual assignment to successors with notice), so we do not redline.

ops.newText: Except as provided in the following sentence, the Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies. ops.text: Section 7.2A Termination for Convenience by the Issuer. In addition to and without limiting the rights set forth in Section 7.2, the Issuer may terminate the rights and obligations of the Servicer (including in its capacity as Custodian) under this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, at any time and without cause, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, the Parent Support Provider, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee. No termination fee, penalty or other compensation will be payable by the Issuer in connection with such termination, other than Servicing Fees accrued and unpaid for services performed through the effective date of termination, and the Servicer will refund to the Issuer any amounts prepaid in respect of the period after such effective date. Any such termination will become effective on the date stated in the notice of termination, but not before a Successor Servicer has accepted its engagement under Section 7.4, and Sections 7.3, 7.4 and 7.5 will apply to any termination under this Section 7.2A.

quote: (c) Removal. If a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing, the Indenture Trustee may and, if directed by the Noteholders of a majority of the Note Balance of the Controlling Class, must remove the Servicer and terminate its rights and obligations under this Agreement by notifying the Servicer, the Issuer, the Parent Support Provider, the Owner Trustee, and the Secured Parties.
rationale: Counterparty side is better than our preferred position: Section 7.1 bars Cellco from resigning as Servicer except where legally unable to perform, and Section 7.3 requires it to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement, so there is no Vendor termination-for-convenience right. However, on our side the only route to remove the Servicer is Section 7.2(c) for a Servicer Termination Event (i.e. for cause), and the Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated (Section 8.3) — well beyond 12 months. The Optional Acquisition/Clean-Up Redemption (Section 8.1) and Optional Redemption (Section 8.2) are held by the Class A Certificateholder, defined as "the Originators or their designee" (counterparty-side), and require agreement on the Optional Acquisition Amount, so they are not a customer convenience exit. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months fails the fallback, so we have added a 30-day no-fee convenience termination right, conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement under Section 7.4 to preserve servicing continuity for the Noteholders.

Noted only for the record: the review right we hold is exercisable at the Servicer's offices and is subject to Cellco's security, confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies, which is customary for this deal type.

quote: From time to time, the Class A Certificateholder may, solely at its option, deposit amounts into the Acquisition Account, as set forth in Section 2.5 of the Trust Agreement.
rationale: The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction on the Issuer or Depositor, so it sits at the preferred position (no minimum commitment; consideration is paid only for property actually transferred). The closest analogues all cut in our favour or are purely optional: (i) transfers of Additional Receivables under Section 2.1(b)-(d) are conditional (Transfer Notice, Credit Enhancement Test, Pool Composition Tests, Depositor certifications) and consideration equals the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount for receivables actually acquired — the Issuer is nowhere obliged to acquire a minimum volume; (ii) funding of the Acquisition Account and the related Negative Carry Account under Section 4.4(d)(i) and 4.4(c)(i) is made by the Class A Certificateholder "solely at its option", and Required Acquisition Deposit Amount / Required Negative Carry Amount are only internal cash-trapping levels with excesses released back to the Certificateholders, not payments we must make to the counterparty; (iii) the Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption in Article VIII are options, not obligations, and require full payment of the Notes; and (iv) the only "shortfall" mechanic (Section 4.3(h) Credit Payments) is an obligation of the Marketing Agent to fund us. The $425,000 Additional Successor Servicer Fee floor is a servicing-transition fee for a replacement servicer, not a purchase commitment, and it supports our ability to replace Cellco. No redline required.

The cited text supports the conclusion: Section 2.1(b)/(d) transfers of Additional Receivables are condition-based with consideration tied to receivables actually acquired, so no minimum volume is imposed on the Issuer/Depositor. Acquisition Account and Negative Carry Account funding (Sections 4.4(d)(i) and 4.4(c)(i)) is expressly made by the Class A Certificateholder 'solely at its option', and the Article VIII Optional Acquisition/Clean-Up Redemption is an option, not an obligation — neither is take-or-pay against us. The only 'shortfall' language (Section 4.3(h) Credit Payments) runs in our favour, obliging the Marketing Agent/Originator to deposit funds, correctly excluded under the rule's guidance that commitments made to us are fine. Rationale correctly notes the $425,000 Additional Successor Servicer Fee floor is a servicing-transition fee, not a purchase commitment, so it is not a MINCOMMIT deviation; no deterministic check failures and no over-flagging.

quote: The Servicer will not be obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, procedures, models, servicing software or other applications to any Successor Servicer or any third party, or provide anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies.
rationale: Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ" and "induce" return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant anywhere in the Agreement. Article VII (Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer), including the transition provisions in Sections 7.4 and 7.5, imposes only cooperation and records/funds-transfer duties on the outgoing Servicer, plus a carve-out preserving Cellco's proprietary processes and software; nothing restricts the Issuer, the Depositor, the Indenture Trustee or any Successor Servicer from soliciting or hiring Cellco servicing personnel on a Servicer transition. Article IX (Other Agreements) likewise contains no restrictive covenant of this kind. This meets the preferred position (no non-solicit binding our party), so no redline is proposed.

verification.notes: The rule's preferred position is the absence of any non-solicit binding the Customer; the cited transition provisions (Sections 7.4/7.5) impose only cooperation and records/funds-transfer duties and contain no solicit/hire/induce covenant, so 'compliant' is the correct classification. Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline was proposed and no comment was added — the rendered text is identical to the original paragraphs, which is the expected output. The failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, general-solicitation carve-out) are artifacts of there being no non-solicit clause to measure; they do not indicate a substantive defect here. Cited paragraphs are relevant evidence of absence (post-termination transition duties are the most likely home for such a covenant), and the rationale accurately notes the proprietary-process carve-out does not restrict hiring of Servicer personnel.

quote: Section 8.3 Termination. This Agreement will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a) the date upon which the last remaining Receivable is paid in full, settled, sold or written off and any amounts received are applied and (b) the Issuer is terminated under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement.
rationale: This is a securitization transfer and servicing agreement with no subscription term, renewal term or evergreen mechanic. Article VIII fixes a single, self-liquidating term: the Agreement terminates automatically on the earlier of the last Receivable being paid in full/settled/sold/written off or termination of the Issuer under Section 8.1 of the Trust Agreement, with Sections 8.1 and 8.2 giving the Class A Certificateholder optional acquisition/redemption exits. Searches for "renew", "automatically renew", "successive", "extended for" and "unless either party gives notice" return no results, so there is no automatic renewal, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price-uplift language. There is nothing to shorten or cap, and no exit risk to us as Issuer/Depositor (the Servicer cannot roll the term forward unilaterally). The auto-renewal rule is therefore inapplicable to this deal structure rather than breached; no redline proposed.

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which matches the rendered output (p0363 is unchanged) — consistent with the expectation that compliant findings carry no negotiation edit. The cited text supports the rationale: Section 8.3 sets a single self-liquidating term (last Receivable paid/settled/sold/written off, or termination of the Issuer under the Trust Agreement) with no evergreen, successive-term, notice-window or price-uplift mechanic. Absence of any auto-renewal or non-renewal notice window is favorable to our side (the Servicer cannot unilaterally roll the term forward), so treating the rule as satisfied rather than flagging a deviation avoids over-flagging; classifying as 'missing' would be inappropriate because this securitization transfer and servicing structure does not contemplate a subscription renewal clause. The failed deterministic check ('non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days — number not found') is expected here: there is no notice window to measure, so the regex miss is not evidence of a defect. Rationale is accurate and appropriately scoped as internal evaluation evidence; no actionable redline was required or proposed.

quote: (a) Cooperation on Termination. On its resignation or termination, the Servicer will cooperate with the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in effecting (i) the termination of its rights and obligations under this Agreement and (ii) an orderly transition of such rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer.
rationale: A usable exit/transition regime exists and clears the fallback. Section 7.5 requires the outgoing Servicer to cooperate in an orderly transition (7.5(a)), to transfer all funds and to deliver the Receivable Files and the accounts and records it maintains to the Successor Servicer as soon as practicable after the effective date of resignation or termination (7.5(b)), and to bear all reasonable transition expenses of the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and Successor Servicer (7.5(c)) — i.e. transition assistance at the Servicer's cost rather than at its then-current rates, which is better than the preferred position for us. Section 7.3 requires Cellco to continue performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement (and to continue remittance obligations under 3.12(b) while any Receivable has a Principal Balance), so assistance runs well beyond 90 days/6 months. Section 3.10(f) separately requires the Custodian to deliver the Receivable Files to the Indenture Trustee or successor custodian on termination of its custodial appointment, again at the terminated custodian's expense. Walk-away territory (no data return, or immediate deletion) is not present. Minor sub-elements short of the model language, noted but not redlined: file/record delivery is "as soon as practicable" rather than a hard 30-day deadline; there is no deletion-and-certification mechanic (unsurprising here, since Cellco remains Marketing Agent/Administrator and needs Obligor data to bill the underlying accounts); and 7.5(b) carves out the Servicer's proprietary processes, models and servicing software and items restricted by confidentiality or privacy policies. We would raise the 30-day delivery outside date only as a low-priority comment.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
sectionRef: § VII SERVICER RESIGNATION AND TERMINATION; SUCCESSOR SERVICER

verification.notes: The cited text substantively supports the compliant classification: §7.5(a) requires cooperation in an orderly transition, §7.5(b) requires transfer of funds and delivery of the Receivable Files and records to the Successor Servicer, §7.5(c) puts transition expenses on the outgoing Servicer, and §7.3 keeps the Servicer performing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement — assistance and data return are present and exceed the fallback duration. Walk-away territory (no data return, or immediate deletion of data) is absent; §3.10(f) adds a parallel file-delivery obligation for the Custodian at its own expense. The failed deterministic 'data return/transition present' regex is a phrasing artifact — this ABS agreement uses 'Receivable Files', 'accounts and records' and 'Successor Servicer' rather than 'data export/return' vocabulary — so it does not undercut the substance. Shortfalls versus the model language ('as soon as practicable' rather than a hard 30-day outside date, no deletion-and-certification mechanic, carve-outs for proprietary servicing software and confidentiality/privacy-restricted items) are correctly noted in the rationale as minor sub-elements rather than flagged as a deviation, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics. No redline or counterparty comment is proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding retained as internal evidence.

quote: (a) General Servicing Obligations. The Servicer will manage, service, administer and collect on the Receivables with reasonable care using that degree of skill and attention that the Servicer exercises for all comparable device payment plan agreement receivables that it services for itself or others according to the Servicing Procedures.
rationale: The transaction contains the functional equivalent of the performance warranty package and it meets (indeed exceeds) the preferred position on the material terms. Quality standard: Section 3.2(a) binds Cellco as Servicer to service with reasonable care using the degree of skill and attention it applies to comparable receivables it services for itself or others under the Servicing Procedures — the securitization analogue of "professional and workmanlike." Conformance warranty and duration: the Eligibility Representation is made by each Originator and the Servicer as of the Closing Date and each Acquisition Date and expressly "will survive the transfer and absolute assignment of the Receivables" and the pledge to the Indenture Trustee (p0069/p0071), as do the Servicer's and Marketing Agent's Section 6.1 representations (p0257) — i.e., open-ended survival rather than the preferred 12-month/90-day windows. Remedy: Section 2.5(b)-(c) requires the Originator to reacquire, or the Servicer to acquire, any Receivable for which the Eligibility Representation was breached (uncured, material adverse effect), and Section 3.3(b) requires the Servicer to acquire Receivables where it fails to cure a breach of its Section 3.2(c)/(d) obligations, in each case at the Acquisition Amount (present value of the Principal Balance net of collections) — a cash refund-equivalent remedy after a cure period, which satisfies the "repair, replace or refund" element. Compliance-with-law warranties are present (No Violation / No Conflict). No "AS IS" clause or blanket warranty disclaimer appears anywhere; Section 6.2(a)'s limitation to willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence preserves the parties' "specific obligations," so the reacquisition/acquisition remedy is not swallowed — and that liability standard is a limitation-of-liability point addressed under the LOL rule, not double-flagged here. The absence of documentation-conformance and malicious-code warranties is not material in a receivables transfer and servicing agreement (no software or deliverables). No redline proposed.

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered redline is byte-identical to the original paragraphs, so nothing improper is being proposed to the counterparty. The cited text supports the compliance conclusion: Section 3.2(a) supplies a quality-of-performance standard (reasonable care / degree of skill and attention applied to comparable receivables under the Servicing Procedures), the Eligibility Representation is made at Closing and each Acquisition Date with express survival of transfer and pledge, and Sections 2.5(b)-(c) / 3.3(b)-(d) supply a cash reacquisition/acquisition remedy at the Acquisition Amount after an uncured material breach — the functional analogue of 'repair, replace or refund'. No 'AS IS' clause or blanket warranty disclaimer appears in the cited material, so the walk-away trigger is absent and the express representations are not swallowed. The failed deterministic check (no explicit 90-day/12-month period) is a phrasing artifact of this instrument type: the representations survive open-endedly rather than for a fixed window, which is better than the preferred 12-month/90-day limits for our side, and the rationale expressly notes the point rather than ignoring it. Non-applicable preferred sub-elements (documentation conformance, malicious code) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, and the willful-misconduct/gross-negligence liability standard is properly deferred to the LOL rule instead of being double-flagged here.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Cellco holds the Receivable Files and Obligor personally identifiable information as Servicer and Custodian, but the Agreement contains no insurance covenant, so we have added our standard coverage requirement (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request). ops.text: Section 10.14 Insurance. Cellco, in each of its capacities as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian, will maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000; (c) cyber liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 covering its handling of the Receivable Files and any Personally Identifiable Information of the Obligors; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Cellco will provide certificates of insurance to the Issuer and the Depositor on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 10.14 (Insurance) in Article X requiring Cellco, as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian, to carry CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation coverage and to provide certificates on request.

quote: (e) Access to Receivable Files. The Custodian will give the Servicer access to the Receivable Files and, on request of the Servicer, the Custodian will promptly release any document in the Receivable Files to the Servicer for purposes of servicing the Receivables.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind. A full-text search for "insurance" returns only unrelated references (insurance premiums billed to Obligor accounts at p0095 and FDIC deposit insurance at p0903), and Articles III, VI and X contain no coverage requirement, fidelity bond or errors-and-omissions provision. Meanwhile, Cellco is the counterparty performing services that squarely engage this rule: under Section 3.10 it acts as Custodian and "will hold and maintain in custody" the Receivable Files (p0138), maintains them and the receivables systems on which they are electronically stored (p0141, p0145), and controls access subject to its "confidentiality, privacy and data protection policies" (p0146). The Receivable Files comprise Obligor records, and the Agreement itself recognises Personally Identifiable Information as a category requiring redaction (p0446, p0884). Exhibit A ("Custodian's Security Requirements") is not reproduced in this form (sec-p1043 contains no substantive text), so no coverage requirement sits there either. That places the document in walk-away territory under this rule — no insurance for a vendor that processes personal data — so neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met. Redline inserts a new Section 10.14 in Article X Miscellaneous, per the rule's redline guidance, at the preferred level (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with terminology conformed to this Agreement (Receivable Files, Personally Identifiable Information, Obligors, applicable Law) and applied to Cellco in all three of its capacities. Noting for context: severity is low and insurance covenants are atypical in a securitization transfer and servicing agreement, where Cellco's indemnity under Section 6.3 provides some overlapping (though uncollateralised and gross-negligence-limited) protection; the fallback of E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M is offered in the comment if the full programme is resisted.

verification.notes: Factual predicate holds: the Agreement contains no insurance/fidelity-bond/E&O covenant, and Cellco as Servicer/Custodian holds the Receivable Files and Obligor Personally Identifiable Information (Section 3.10, p0138–p0146), so the rule's trigger (service provider touching our data) is engaged and 'missing' is the correct status — neither preferred nor fallback coverage exists anywhere in the document. Redline is actionable and tracks the model language at the preferred level (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp, certificates on request), inserted as a stand-alone miscellaneous section rather than rewriting existing text, with terminology properly conformed to this Agreement (Receivable Files, Personally Identifiable Information, Obligors, applicable Law) and applied to Cellco in its Servicer/Marketing Agent/Custodian capacities. Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the E&O 1M / cyber 2M fallback, as the tone guidance requires; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and the inserted insurance obligation renders. Minor caveats, not disqualifying: the anchor paragraph (p0439) is a sentence fragment, so confirm the new Section 10.14 lands at the end of a section within Article X rather than mid-clause; and the rationale correctly notes that insurance covenants are atypical in a securitization transfer and servicing agreement (Servicer fidelity/E&O covenants are nonetheless common), which supports keeping this at low severity and negotiating to the fallback if resisted.
